title: dactylis glomerata subsp. merinoana
intro: Dactylis glomerata subsp. merinoana, commonly known as Merino grass, is a subspecies of the Dactylis glomerata plant, which belongs to the family Poaceae. This perennial grass is native to the Mediterranean region and has been used for centuries in traditional medicine due to its numerous health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial properties. The health benefits of Merino grass are attributed to its therapeutic actions, such as soothing digestive issues, reducing fever, and alleviating respiratory problems. The bioactive constituents of Merino grass include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
